what: Interleaved A/B/C measurement of Flight do_get (bypass arm) across three release binaries, with a byte-identical bare-scan drift control in every run. THE ONLY comparison this session licenses: no absolute here is reusable cross-session.

L4.description: BASE + lever 4 (state the Flight encoder's re-slicing target)

L46.description: BASE + lever 4 + lever 6 (build the egress Arrow schema once per merge)

design.binaries: three separately built --release cqlite-flight binaries, verified distinct by md5 at run time and swapped in per run; the md5 digests themselves were NOT captured into the run artifacts and the staged copies no longer exist, so they are NOT recoverable and are NOT restated here (rig gap — record the binary digest in results.json)
design.reps: 1 rep per arm per round, 10 rounds per arm, 30 runs total
design.rotation: arm order rotated per round with period 3 (BASE/L4/L46 -> L4/L46/BASE -> L46/BASE/L4), so no arm holds a fixed position in the round

sessions.continuity: one continuous session, nothing else running on the box

design.drift_control: the bare-scan arm (execute_streaming) is CODE-IDENTICAL in all three arms - neither lever touches the scan path (lever 4 is cqlite-flight only; lever 6's cqlite-core half adds a schema-reuse entry point in export/arrow_convert.rs that the bare scan never calls) - so its 30 readings are a within-session drift control, not a measurement of the change. NOT literally byte-identical: ws0-scan-bench links cqlite-core, so the L46 arm's copy differs in bytes. The empirical check is per_arm_bare_scan_control_median_rows_per_sec below, which agrees to within 0.25%.

corpus.note: CQLite-written + CQLite-read: PERFORMANCE FIXTURE ONLY (#3042), never a correctness oracle

conclusion.ac1: UNMET - re-anchored to issue #3248 (attribute inside the unattributed encode region before any array-build lever is funded); lever 1 routes to #3231
conclusion.spec_r5: a correctly measured, correctly reported negative result IS a satisfying outcome of this change (openspec/changes/arrow-encode-doget/specs/arrow-encode-doget/spec.md)

discarded_attempt.verdict: DISCARDED IN FULL - no number from it is used anywhere
discarded_attempt.design: first interleaved attempt at the lever-4 comparison: two arms (A=BASE, B=L4), 1 rep per arm per round, alternating
discarded_attempt.why: a concurrent cargo release build landed on the pinned server cores mid-attempt. The signature is in the counters: flight IPC 1.516 (A-1) -> 1.442 (B-1) -> 1.458 (A-2) with cycles/row 24,088 -> 26,068 -> 25,914, i.e. cycles inflated ~8% while rows/s fell ~4% - foreign cycles being counted inside a CPU-wide (-C 2,10) window. The attempt was aborted mid-round-2 (B-2 has no results.json) and re-run from scratch as ab3/ab3b after the build finished.
discarded_attempt.supporting_evidence: target/release/deps holds cqlite_core/cqlite_flight/flight_loadgen release artifacts stamped 06:38:23-06:40:30 UTC, i.e. a rustc/cargo release build resident on the box across the tail of this attempt (rustc writes its outputs at the END of compilation, so a 06:38 artifact was being produced during the 06:32-06:38 runs). The attribution to cargo is the operator's contemporaneous call plus these timestamps; it is not an independently instrumented per-CPU trace.
discarded_attempt.lesson: the bare-scan drift control did NOT move during the contamination (335,679 / 332,270 / 335,540 rows/s - all normal): its ~12 s window escaped the interference that hit the ~57 s Flight window. So the byte-identical drift control is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT; what flagged this was the IPC + cycles/row signature on the measured arm. Watch both.

review_remeasurement_2026_08_03.why: The #3096 review found FLIGHT_DATA_SIZE_TARGET_BYTES equalled GRPC_DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES with a `<=` guard admitting it. The target moved to 4,063,232 B (ceiling - 64 KiB framing reserve - 64 KiB inexactness margin), which changes framing geometry, so lever 4's recorded +4,817 rows/s / +2.3% / -441 cycles/row (measured AT the superseded 4 MiB target) was no longer certified and is SUPERSEDED by this session.

arms.NOTGT: HEAD with the with_max_flight_data_size call REMOVED (inherits arrow-flight 53.4.1's 2 MiB default) - the true lever-4 isolation on SHIPPED code
arms.L4P: HEAD as shipped: encoder target 4,063,232 B (3.875 MiB)

design.session: 2026-08-03 16:19-16:59 UTC, one continuous session, nothing else on the box

bare_scan_drift_control_all_24_runs.note: the 8.0% rows/s spread is driven by ONE run (L4P-7, 331,886 rows/s); over the other 23 runs the control spread is 3.6% (347,355..360,405, median 358,019). Recorded, not trimmed: the outlier stays in every median above.

conclusion.lever4_at_the_shipped_target: MEASURED AT ZERO. Paired within-round median -72.2 rows/s (-0.03%), 4 of 8 rounds positive - far inside the 5.5-9.8% per-arm spread.
conclusion.superseded_figure: +4,817 rows/s (+2.3%) / -441 cycles/row, measured at the SUPERSEDED 4 MiB target in the 10-round session above. NOT the delivered figure and not restated as one.
conclusion.cumulative_vs_base: -573.1 rows/s (-0.25%), 3 of 8 rounds positive - also indistinguishable from zero.
conclusion.cycles_per_row: lever 4' does reduce cycles/row by a median 136.9 (~0.6%) with rows/s unmoved. Per spec R1 that is NOT reported as a throughput win: a profile improvement with unmoved rows/s is explicitly not evidence of a gain.
conclusion.what_survives: lever 4's positively verified effect is FRAMING (fewer FlightData messages, no degenerate 1-row tails) plus wire safety at the reserved ceiling, both asserted in-repo by cqlite-flight/src/streaming_framing_tests.rs. It is retained for wire safety, not for throughput.
conclusion.ac1: UNMET, and by a wider margin in this session: control median 357,790 rows/s / do_get 230,321 rows/s = ratio 1.553x; AC1 target 275,223 rows/s; shortfall -44,902 rows/s (-16.3%). Re-anchored to #3248.
conclusion.cross_session_absolutes: this session's control (357,790 rows/s) sits ~7% above the main session's (332,970). Same box, same corpus, same bytes, 9 hours apart - the one rule this record exists to enforce, observed a second time.
